title: A Copilot Waits to Be Asked: Why the Manual Middle of a Mortgage Needs an Agent That Holds the Goal, and How You Bound What It Does
summary: A copilot's ceiling is the number of hours your staff spend asking it things, which is exactly the resource a mortgage operation is short of. The work that actually clogs a loan runs for days and nobody is sitting there prompting it. What changes when an agent holds the goal instead of answering a question, and the specific controls that keep an autonomous agent inside a boundary an examiner will accept, under SR 11-7 and ECOA.
